4.45.betting_forecast: 2/1 Central Command, 9/4 Fallacious Promise, 7/1 Project Kinsman, 8/1 Skirt Around, 12/1 Ballon Rouge, Steel Fixer, Sweet
4.45.spotlight_verdict: Phil Kirby saddles a couple with chances and it will be interesting to see how Skirt Around, who's undergone wind surgery since last running, goes in the market. Central Command ought to do better in first-time headgear, having been gelded, but FALLACIOUS PROMISE (nap) should be suited by tonight's stiffer test, having come home nicely over 1m when last seen.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Beaten a long way on her Wolverhampton handicap debut early last month but didn't look to see out 1m4f having gone to the front off the home turn; 4lb lower and she ought to fare better.
Half-brother to three winners, including on Tapeta; gelded since well held in three 7f runs at Kempton late last year (big prices each time); goes in first-time headgear and this is more realistic.

First signs of life when coming home strongly, upped to 1m, for second in a Kempton 0-55 in February (race worked out fairly among the principals); stamina not assured on pedigree, upped 3lb, but his claims are obvious otherwise for a yard enjoying a good spring.
horses.breeding: b g Lope Y Fernandez - Byrony

horses.spotlight_comment: Better on her C&D handicap debut here 18 days ago, upped from 7f, and is 1lb lower tonight; winner and third that night have let the side down since but that gave something to build on.

Huge prices and well beaten in three runs last autumn; this more realistic back from seven months off, now handicapping off a lowly opening mark, but would want to see some support before considering him.

Not without hope in three 7f runs in the space of a few weeks last September, including here, since when she's undergone wind surgery; starts handicap life at a sensible level and the market should tell a tale for a yard also responsible for Project Kinsman.
horses.breeding: gr f Knicks Go - Alotta Skirt

horses.spotlight_comment: Quite well related, being a half-brother to three AW winners; overraced and hit traffic in a messy Wolverhampton handicap (1m4f) on his AW debut ten days ago, but that was at least a step up on his turf efforts.
horses.breeding: b g Too Darn Hot - Tebee

horses.spotlight_comment: Exposed, regressive maiden who again finished weakly on her first crack at 1m4f two months ago; handicapper giving her every chance but she's vulnerable to improvers and not obviously fancied.
horses.breeding: b f Dream Ahead - Party Line

5.20.betting_forecast: 3/1 Say What You See, 6/1 Mao Shang Wong, Star Cast, 8/1 Jujubella, 10/1 Jack Sparowe, Sure And Stedfast, 12/1
5.20.spotlight_verdict: Some sort of case could be made for all of them but the two standouts look to be SAY WHAT YOU SEE, who progressed well in the second half of last year and boasts a good record on Tapeta, and dual C&D winner Star Cast, who found the drop to 1m working against her on turf last time. John Butler's pair Sea The Light and Jack Sparowe also merit consideration.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Patchy during a limited campaign last year for Ed Dunlop; wins as a 3yo came on soft turf and this trip looks a bare minimum for her new yard on comeback.

Stays a deal further but has always liked it here and has run well a couple of times over C&D this year; a good pace would help but finished behind Say What You See on turf last time and others hold stronger claims.

Not as good now and prone to the occasional off-day; still to win over C&D but his record suggests he needs considering off this mark, especially given his two previous runs in cheekpieces both resulted in near-misses.

Scudamore Paul Mulrennan 8-1 71 - 86 Progressive for cheekpieces going on early last year, with three course wins, latterly off a 4lb lower mark; again goes without the headgear back from six months off and there's nothing to suggest she's best caught fresh.

Quite late in the day to be going beyond an extended 1m for the first time; often makes the running and can race freely, so will need to settle early from a wide stall back from ten weeks off; not in much form when last seen either way.
Not seen it out over 1m4f a couple of times since two wins in March, one over C&D; it might just be that his current mark is beyond him but there won't be any excuses tonight.
horses.breeding: b g Too Darn Hot - Moment Of Silence

horses.spotlight_comment: Wins for David O'Meara both came over C&D, including a division of this race two years ago; not beaten far at 100-1 here two months ago but looked flattered in a messy affair and he's generally struggled for this yard.

Two wins and a second from three runs on Tapeta, the second coming when clear with a progressive winner over C&D last August; turned over twice as favourite on turf this spring but holds decent claims once more.

Won a 7f maiden on this card last year on his racecourse debut; struggled subsequently but this is a bit easier down another 3lb in first-time blinkers (wore cheekpieces when last seen); yard also run Jack Sparowe.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Soltada

horses.spotlight_comment: Two C&D wins already this year, latterly off 4lb lower, and continues in form, the drop to 1m working against her when she came home nicely at Doncaster five weeks ago; goes on the shortlist.
Buzzy gelding who won twice on turf last year; only run once before on the AW but this mark should be within range if he keeps calm in a first-time hood back from six months off.

5.53.betting_forecast: 4/5 The Cursor, 3/1 New York Minute, 6/1 Machete, 10/1 Ludo's Landing, 16/1 Havachoc, 33/1 Melinda.
5.53.spotlight_verdict: Three of the four who are running off their correct marks hold no secrets from the handicapper and THE CURSOR, who's lightly raced and open to further improvement having been gelded, is clearly the one with most potential.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won three on Tapeta early in the year, latterly over C&D, but nothing above 0-55 level; consistent since but is effectively 8lb higher than when last successful, being asked to run from 6lb out of the handicap.
horses.breeding: b g Havana Gold - White Chocolate

horses.spotlight_comment: Won for blinkers first being fitted and did so again for them going back on over C&D two months ago; lacked consistency in recent times and there's not much wiggle room off this mark but he's capable if on a going day.
horses.breeding: b m Churchill - Wait And See

horses.spotlight_comment: Not as good now but remains generally consistent and is back on the mark off which he won here (1m2f) in the winter; needs to bounce back from a lesser effort over C&D when last seen six weeks ago.

Scudamore Lexie Clarkson (7) 33-1 66 - - Limited in four runs on the Flat as a 3yo before winning a juvenile hurdle when last seen 18 months ago; this looks quite an ask from 2lb out of the handicap under Lexie Clarkson, who's taking just a second ride under rules.

Headgear helped last autumn, with him landing a hat-trick, including two over 2m round Southwell, latterly off a 4lb lower mark; solid effort there last Thursday, back from a few months off (1m3f), but he'll want a similarly strong pace this evening.

Powerful yard, who won this two years ago, had a few disappoint at short prices of late; this lightly raced 400,000gns yearling holds obvious claims, having been gelded since winning his novice last summer (highly tried a couple of times prior) though.

6.30.betting_forecast: Evs Eklleem, 11/4 Eljowhary, 4/1 Marhayb, 8/1 Viper, 14/1 Record Day, 25/1 Grasmere Boy, 33/1 Khaleejy, 66/1 Thunder Rush,
6.30.spotlight_verdict: Eljowhary and Marhayb are much respected newcomers and second choice Viper showed enough at Doncaster to merit a look. However, EKLLEEM showed clear promise on his second run as a juvenile and the Haggas factor points towards further improvement this year.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: Beaten double-digit lengths in two C&D novices and one for another day.

200,000gns yearling; mixed messages as to what he achieved when well-held second in a 7f Newmarket novice in October but that's still the best form on offer and there should be more to come as a 3yo now gelded.

140,000gns yearling and a half-brother to the useful White Crown Star; dam unraced half-sister to winners Eleonora Duse (1m2f Group 2) and Scottish Stage (1m2f Listed; runner-up in Irish Oaks); has been gelded but he's nicely bred and in top hands.
Refused to race on debut and tailed off when she has completed; had wind surgery.
Fourth foal; dam 7f winner (RPR 93) out of French 1m4f winning half-sister to 1m2f Listed winner Roscius; he'd be a surprise winner.
Cost 75,000euros as a 2yo but never raced for James Tate (withdrawn in late 2024 after getting upset in the stalls; 5-1 at the time); can only be watched making debut as a 5yo.
160,000gns yearling; third foal; half-sister to winners Fire Flame (7f; RPR 82) and Marianglas (7f AW; 74); dam 6f 2yo winner (100); the market could be informative with the owner doubly represented.
Posted modest RPRs when showing some promise in his first two races; looks one for handicaps.
His fifth over 1m here in March was a remote one and he went off at 33-1.
Market springer on his debut at Doncaster a month ago (7f, good to soft) and he shaped nicely in a race dominated by strong yards; open to improvement.

7.02.betting_forecast: 7/4 Dandy Breeze, 5/2 Starmade, 5/1 There's A Chance, 10/1 Numero Vingt, 12/1 Logi Bear, Loquella, 14/1 Stoic Poet, 25/1 Yy
7.02.spotlight_verdict: Starmade and Dandy Breeze still have potential, while Stoic Poet (second choice) could leave his 2yo form behind him this year. THERE'S A CHANCE ran better than her finishing position suggests in a Goodwood conditions event when last seen and she could have more to offer over a stiff 6f. Her Hamilton nursery win worked out well and she is tentatively suggested in a tricky race.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Slowly away when second, beaten a nose, on his debut here in December (5f; 12-1); duly went one better when the odds-on favourite for another 5f novice here in January; gelded afterwards; makes his handicap debut over an extra furlong and off a mark that looks manageable; betting useful.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - Winter Oasis

horses.spotlight_comment: C&D win on debut and then ran well under a penalty at Wolverhampton; dropped away to finish sixth of the seven runners in a 7f handicap at Southwell in March; returning to 6f can help but not obviously well treated.
horses.breeding: b f No Nay Never - Teofilo's Princess

horses.spotlight_comment: Won two 6f events on Polytrack in February; unplaced in both handicaps though and his latest 2lb drop isn't enough to tempt.

Improved with each of his three runs last autumn, getting off the mark in a 5f maiden here in October; plugged on for third in a 5.7f handicap at Bath (good to soft) on his reappearance two weeks ago, beaten nearly 5l at the finish; needs more to defy this mark but returning to AW may help.

No immediate improvement for the switch to handicaps when eighth of nine over 7f at Haydock 216 days ago; his novice and maiden runs had threatened better though and he still has time to fulfil that promise; betting useful in a winnable race.
horses.breeding: ch g Far Above - Wine And Roses

horses.spotlight_comment: Made a successful handicap debut at Hamilton (6f, good) last July off a 6lb lower mark and that form worked out nicely; ran in sales races on her final two starts in 2025, eighth of 21 at Naas and seventh of 14 at Goodwood (7f, good to soft); was challenging 1f out in the latter event before her stamina gave way; untried on AW and absent for 219 days but there could be more to come this year.
horses.breeding: b f Magna Grecia - Dubai Power

horses.spotlight_comment: Off the mark at the fourth attempt when landing a modest fillies' novice over C&D in December; 66-1 and well beaten on last month's stable/handicap debut; best watched.

7.33.betting_forecast: 7/4 Recency Bias, 4/1 Pressure's On, 5/1 The Green Man, 7/1 Beale Street, 12/1 Rich Rhythm, 14/1 Blufferonthebus, Ey Up Its
7.33.spotlight_verdict: The Green Man might not get the strong pace he needs, so attention is turned to PRESSURE'S ON, who is back over his best trip. Recency Bias remains a relative unknown quantity and he could be the danger. Beale Street's last run was poor but he's well capable of being involved too.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: All four wins have been here but over 6f; he appears to stay 7f but had a shocker over C&D last time; that was too bad to be true in fairness.
The last of three wins in 2025 came here off only 1lb lower, albeit in a Class 6; offered little since then.
Realistically weighted on his best efforts last year and his second run in March was better than the first; however, his AW exploits are unconvincing.
horses.breeding: ch g Pastoral Pursuits - Mad Jazz

horses.spotlight_comment: Won a small-field C&D handicap over Christmas but two nothing runs in January and difficult to know what to expect from him after a break.

Didn't appear to be crying out for the return to 1m at Doncaster and weakened late on; this is his trip, over which he was twice runner-up at Wolverhampton in March; not handicapped out of it, either.

Won his novice here by 5l and looked on a workable mark for his handicap debut at Wolverhampton but he never travelled after starting slowly; wouldn't judge him on that performance and could be given another chance.
Again he was slowly away when never dangerous here a month ago; inconsistent no matter how he breaks and, although capable off this mark, he comes with risks.
horses.breeding: b g Profitable - Gift Of Music

horses.spotlight_comment: Close up behind Beale Street here in March (6f) and produced a similar effort from off the pace to be runner-up over C&D 11 days ago; needs a good pace to chase (stays 1m) and no guarantee that he'll get one here.
Prolific here during the 2024/25 AW season but he's beaten one rival in two starts after an absence; couldn't support with any confidence.
horses.breeding: b g Sioux Nation - Two Pass

8.10.betting_forecast: 6/4 Caragio, 5/1 Raft Up, 8/1 Kings Merchant, 10/1 Lion's House, Speeding Bullet, 12/1 Asadjumeirah, Lord Abama, 16/1 Annie
8.10.spotlight_verdict: The fact he hung under pressure at Chelmsford raises a note of caution at the likely odds but CARAGIO looked well ahead of his mark at Yarmouth ten days ago and he can make light of his penalty. Raft Up, another penalised runner, may be best of the rest but Kings Merchant and the returning Speeding Bullet are others to consider.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Heavy ground excuses her low-key end to 2025 and she ran a series of good races, including a win at Hamilton when first tried in blinkers; whether first time out is the time to catch her remains to be seen but interesting that a tongue-tie goes on for her return.
Five-time C&D winner; unable to justify favouritism in a 0-55 here 11 days ago and he has more on his plate at this level.
horses.breeding: b g Adaay - Place In My Heart

horses.spotlight_comment: Recorded back-to-back C&D wins last October (the second off 3lb lower) but the wheels came off in his hat-trick bid in November; back from 161 days off with a point to prove.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - Rouge Noir

horses.spotlight_comment: Began his 3yo campaign with a BHA mark of 93; a lot of water has flowed under the bridge since but he has bounced back to form for Adam Kirby, finishing second at Chelmsford in March (7f) before an easy win at Yarmouth ten days ago (6f, good to firm); 3lb well in under a penalty; obvious chance.

Finished a creditable third of seven (6f, good to soft; RPR 66) at Ayr on his 2yo debut; well beaten twice afterwards (7f and 1m); makes handicap and stable debut after a 506-day absence; has been gelded; betting to guide.
horses.breeding: b g Ten Sovereigns - Madeira Moon

horses.spotlight_comment: Won a 7f handicap at Catterick off this mark last July but it has been downhill ever since; plenty to prove.
horses.breeding: gr f Invincible Army - Satwa Ruby

horses.spotlight_comment: On a dangerous mark now and his three runs this year have offered hope that his losing run could be snapped imminently; effective on AW and likely to be involved.
horses.breeding: b g Bated Breath - Rhossili Down

horses.spotlight_comment: C&D winner; popped up in a 5f handicap here in February but more to prove after lesser efforts here (bled from the nose) and on turf on his last two starts.
Two-time C&D winner; unplaced but ran with credit in two Thirsk handicaps last month; type to pop up soon off a reduced mark.

Good efforts in all three 6f runs this year, placed behind the prolific Yorkshire Glory twice and readily seeing off five rivals at Southwell eight days ago; 1lb well in under a penalty; should go well.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - Chicago Fall

horses.spotlight_comment: Reinvented as a sprinter by Paul Midgley last season, winning a 6f handicap at Pontefract in July and turning in three solid efforts over 6f and 5f afterwards; returns from 238 days off but he still has handicapping scope; market confidence would look significant.
horses.breeding: b g Inns Of Court - Shoshoni Wind
